summary: The About page tells the story of the family shop and is the best trust content the site has: founded 1987 on Brook Street, run by the family's daughter, products from small local makers. It is plain text beside a small shop picture, and it ends without a next step. Most important: keep the story, give it room and a link to the shop and the products.
audience: New customers deciding whether to trust an online shop they don't know.
tasks: Find out who is behind the shop

purpose.clear.evidence: „Millbrook Home & Garden was started in 1987 by Peter and Margaret Hartley…“ in the first lines.

purpose.tasks.evidence: The story is there, but the page doesn't link to the shop's address or opening hours.

content.complete.evidence: History, who runs it today, what they stand for.

structure.scannable.evidence: No subheadings; the values („good quality products, fair prices and friendly service“) are hidden in the second paragraph.

action.primary.evidence: No link or button at the end of the page.

nav.menu.evidence: Seven green tabs (Home … Sale!) plus a second department list in the sidebar; the current tab is marked yellow, but Delivery, Returns and Contact live only in the footer.

visual.brand.evidence: The green house-and-leaf logo with the italic Millbrook wordmark, dark green #2f5420 / #4c7f2f and cream surfaces: recognisable on every page and fitting for a home and garden shop. Verdana 11 px is just old, not brand.

visual.images.evidence: The shopfront picture shows the real shop.

visual.hierarchy.evidence: Heading, picture and text in a clear order.

visual.consistency.evidence: Same frame, nav, sidebar boxes and footer as the other pages.

trust.signals.evidence: Family names, founding year, team size and local makers: real reasons to trust.

inventory.why: Out of date and not about the customer.

keep: Founded 1987 by Peter and Margaret Hartley
Good quality, fair prices, friendly service
add: Link to the shop's address and to the departments
design_input: Visit the shop block with a link
